population_estimates.note: Ethiopian highlands under Zagwe rule; medieval Ethiopian demography is poorly documented.

description: Christian Ethiopian dynasty (1137–1270) of Agaw origin that ruled the northern Ethiopian highlands in the interval between the long Aksumite decline and the Solomonic restoration; the Zagwe shifted the political centre south from Aksum to Roha (renamed Lalibela after their most famous king), and during the reign of King Lalibela (c. 1181–1221) commissioned the rock-hewn churches of Lalibela that survive as the dynasty's defining monument and as one of the masterpieces of medieval Christian architecture; the dynasty's claims to descent from Moses's grandson Akizana were always contested, and in 1270 a member of the Solomonic line, Yekuno Amlak, overthrew the last Zagwe king Yetbarak, founding the Solomonic dynasty that would rule Ethiopia until 1974.

temporal.notes: Christian Ethiopian dynasty between the Aksumite empire's collapse and the Solomonic Ethiopian restoration; centred on Lalibela in the highland north.

lifecycle_phases.description: Mara Takla Haymanot displaces the last Aksumite ruler; capital established at Roha in the central highlands; the dynasty consolidates control of the Christian north.
Reign of King Lalibela; commissioning of the rock-hewn monolithic churches at Roha (renamed Lalibela in his honour); contact with the Crusader states and Coptic Patriarchate of Alexandria.
Yekuno Amlak of the Solomonic line overthrows Yetbarak with the support of the monastic establishment; the Zagwe accept the new dynasty in exchange for retaining the Lasta region as a sub-kingdom.
